repo.description:
## Impact

The Gmail (v1) and Brevo nodes passed message content to the mail composer without ensuring it was a string. An expression resolving to an object could carry a `path` or `href` property, which the composer used to read a local file or fetch a URL and attach the result to the outgoing message. An authenticated user able to run a workflow could read any file the n8n process could access or reach an internal address.

## Patches

The issue has been fixed in n8n versions 1.123.73, 2.35.4, and 2.36.2. Users should upgrade to one of these versions or later to remediate the vulnerability.

## Workarounds

If upgrading is not immediately possible, administrators should consider the following temporary mitigations:
- Restrict n8n instance access to fully trusted users only.
- Disable the Gmail node by adding `n8n-nodes-base.gmail` to the `NODES_EXCLUDE` environment variable.
- Ensure the n8n process runs under a dedicated low-privilege OS user account to limit the impact of any file access.

These workarounds do not fully remediate the risk and should only be used as short-term mitigation measures.
repo.summary: Gmail and Brevo nodes accept non-string content, enabling local file read and SSRF
